title: Russia's Largest Multi-Weapon Air Attack: 731 Missiles & Drones — Kyiv Apartment Block Demolished, 7 Killed, 33 Injured
detail: Russia launched its most diverse aerial attack package of the war on the night of May 13–14, 2026: 731 total aerial assets including 675 Shahed-type UAVs, 35 Kh-101 cruise missiles, 18 Iskander-M ballistic missiles, and 3 Kh-47M2 Kinzhal hypersonic missiles — the latter marking the rare simultaneous use of hypersonic, cruise, and ballistic platforms in one wave. Ukraine's air defenses destroyed 41 missiles and 652 drones out of the total wave. In Kyiv, 6 city districts and 6 Kyiv region districts were struck — a residential apartment block was demolished, killing at least 7 people, with 11 rescued from the rubble. At least 33 were injured across the capital including a 2-month-old infant. Other cities struck included Kharkiv, Odesa, Sumy, Bila Tserkva, and Kremenchuk. In the broader 30-hour bombardment spanning May 13–14, Zelensky reported more than 1,560 total drones and missiles launched — the largest sustained aerial campaign of the war. Russia used Gerbera, Italmas, and Banderol loitering munitions as well as Parodiya decoy drones in the strike package. Missiles were fired from Lipetsk, Bryansk, Kursk, and Vologda oblasts; drones launched from Bryansk, Oryol, Millerovo, Primorsko-Akhtarsk, and occupied Crimea.

media.caption: Russia launches 731 aerial assets — Kyiv apartment block demolished, 7 killed, May 14, 2026

title: 187 Combat Engagements — Pokrovsk & Huliaipole Most Active; Russian Losses Pass 1,345,240
detail: Ukraine's General Staff reported 187 total combat engagements in the 24 hours leading into May 14, 2026 — among the highest counts since the ceasefire collapse. The Pokrovsk sector was most active with nearly 50 Russian assault attempts on Ukrainian positions; the Huliaipole sector (Zaporizhzhia Oblast) also saw approximately 50 attacks, including an ambush by a Russian infiltration group on Ukraine's 225th Assault Regiment that killed 2 Ukrainian defenders. Zaporizhzhia region endured 973 Russian strikes on 49 settlements in the preceding 24 hours. Russia also launched 80+ aerial bombs and 30+ airstrikes. Russian cumulative personnel losses reached approximately 1,345,240 — including 1,060 killed or wounded in the 24-hour period. Ukraine intercepted 286 of its own drones that Russia claims to have shot down over 14 Russian regions including Belgorod, Bryansk, Kursk, Rostov, and the Black Sea. Russia's Belgorod governor confirmed 1 man died from injuries sustained in a Ukrainian drone strike.

media.caption: CNN: Russia's winning streak in Ukraine is over — 187 combat engagements, May 14, 2026

title: Kremlin Demands Ceasefire-First Framework — Zelensky: 'Not Actions of Those Who Think War Is Ending'
detail: On May 14, 2026, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov outlined Russia's conditions for renewed negotiations: a ceasefire must be agreed first, followed by a corridor toward full-scale peace talks — directly contradicting Ukraine's insistence that security guarantees must precede any ceasefire. Zelensky responded to continued Russian strikes: 'These are definitely not the actions of those who believe the war is coming to an end.' Peace talks remained at an impasse, with NYT assessing negotiations had effectively failed; Washington's diplomatic attention had shifted toward Iran. Ukraine's Foreign Minister Sybiha reiterated that no territorial concessions would be accepted without binding NATO or equivalent security guarantees. Russia continued demanding cession of the remainder of Donetsk Oblast — the core sticking point. CNN published a major analysis on May 14 concluding 'Russia's winning streak in Ukraine is over,' citing territorial stabilization after months of Russian gains and Ukraine's expanding long-range strike reach. The analysis noted that Russia had suffered a net territorial loss in April 2026 — its first since August 2024.

media.caption: Kremlin sets ceasefire-first conditions as Zelensky condemns ongoing Russian bombardment, May 14, 2026
